PAGINATION-01 Native Baseline

This fixture uses ordinary HTML wrappers. The paired fixture changes only the wrapper element names.

Card 1

Print layout should remain governed by CSS fragmentation rather than by the wrapper tag name.

The content is intentionally long enough to create natural page pressure without assigning synthetic page coordinates.

Card 2

Semantic content remains ordinary headings and paragraphs. Only layout intent is abstracted.

Each card requests break-inside avoidance so browser pagination has a meaningful fragmentation decision to make.

Second section

Card 3

The experiment compares print-media geometry in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

Actual paginated PDF equivalence is additionally checked in Chromium, whose automation API exposes PDF generation.

Card 4

A passing result does not prove all custom elements are pagination-neutral. It supports this deliberately passive light-DOM wrapper model.

Later experiments add columns, sidebars, tables, artwork, and named page profiles independently.

Third section

Card 5

The library should expose document intent while leaving the browser or publishing engine responsible for actual page construction.

This separation is the architectural claim being challenged by the first experiment.

Card 6

Font fallback, browser differences, and long-document behavior remain separate risks and are intentionally not collapsed into one result.

The evidence record must retain those limitations even if this fixture passes.
